name: AutoGuide (Automated Generation and Selection of Context-Aware Guidelines for LLM Agents)
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); preprint arXiv:2403.08978
authors_affiliation: Yao Fu (University of Michigan), Dong-Ki Kim (LG AI Research; equal contribution), Jaekyeom Kim, Sungryull Sohn, Lajanugen Logeswaran, Kyunghoon Bae (LG AI Research), Honglak Lee (University of Michigan and LG AI Research). Primary affiliations: University of Michigan and LG AI Research.
code_url: N/A (no official first-party code repository located on arXiv, OpenReview, the NeurIPS page, or the LG AI Research publication page as of June 2026) [uncertain]
task_domain: Sequential decision-making for LLM agents: embodied household tasks (ALFWorld), web navigation / web shopping (WebShop, WebArena-Reddit), and multi-modal real-world web navigation (GitHub, Google Flights, Coursera).
problem_setting: Interactive sequential decision-making (POMDP) with prompt-based (closed-source) LLM agents. AutoGuide operates in two phases: (1) an OFFLINE knowledge-distillation phase that mines a fixed set of context-aware guidelines from a pre-collected offline dataset of trajectories (collected via ReAct/Reflexion runs or human demonstrations); and (2) an interactive TEST-time phase where the frozen guideline store is retrieved per state to augment the agent prompt. Single-agent. Supervision is weak/automatic: trajectory returns (rewards/success) are used to form contrastive success/failure pairs; no gradient training of the agent or a retriever is performed. Train and test tasks are non-overlapping.
what_is_retrieved: State-conditional natural-language guidelines (conditional 'when context X, do Y' rules) distilled from contrasting success/failure trajectory pairs; each guideline is keyed by a generated natural-language 'context' (a concise description of the agent's current state).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory that is induced offline then FROZEN. The retrievable store (the context-aware guideline dictionary G) is constructed from the agent's own offline experiences (not a static external KB/docs/API corpus), but it is fixed before test time and does not grow during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k selection: after keying into the guideline dictionary by the matched context, an LLM selection module returns the top-k most relevant guidelines (k held fixed, e.g. k=2 in main experiments; k=3 best in the WebShop ablation). Not a completeness-recovery or precision-driven variable-size objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (context-keyed dictionary lookup + LLM top-k selection). Reuse: yes (selected guidelines injected into the action-generation prompt). Revise: no (no per-case adaptation/revision of a retrieved guideline at test time; guidelines used as-is, though an optional grounding module re-aligns guidelines for the out-of-domain transfer experiment). Retain: no at test time (the store is frozen; retention only happens once during offline induction). Flags: [Retrieve=yes, Reuse=yes, Revise=no, Retain=no(at test time)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself around 'context-aware guidelines' distilled from contrastive offline experiences and does not explicitly cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or describe itself as case-based reasoning; it realizes CBR-like retrieve-and-reuse mechanisms under the 'guideline' framing. (Included in group D_case_based_planning by the survey, not by the authors.)
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule: a single concise conditional natural-language guideline ('When on the Reddit main page, if you want to navigate to a specific forum, you should click ...'), organized in a dictionary under a generated state 'context' key. Effectively a state-aware rule abstracted from contrastive (success vs failure) sub-trajectories.
index_source: Growing memory, offline-induced then frozen: guidelines are induced offline from contrastive trajectory pairs in a training task set (e.g., first 100 ALFWorld training tasks; 50 sampled WebShop training tasks) and stored in a context-keyed dictionary; the store is not extended at test time.
index_structure_topology: Metadata/context-keyed dictionary: a dictionary G mapping a generated natural-language 'context' (key) to the set of guidelines applicable in that context (value). An LLM-based context-matching step deduplicates/merges semantically equivalent contexts during construction. No vector index, no graph; a context-keyed associative store.
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever. Retrieval is performed entirely by LLM modules: a context-identification module abstracts the current trajectory into a context, an LLM context-matching check maps it to an existing dictionary key, and an LLM guideline-selection module ranks/selects the top-k guidelines. No BM25/dense embedding retriever is used.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / prompted LLM). No retriever is trained. The guideline-generation pipeline is supervised only indirectly by trajectory return labels used to form contrastive success/failure pairs (R(tau+) > R(tau-)); the context-identification, context-matching, and selection modules are zero/few-shot-prompted LLMs, not learned retrievers.
query_construction: Thought/state-conditioned: at each timestep the context-identification module M_context summarizes the current partial trajectory tau_:t (observations + actions so far) into a concise natural-language 'context'. That generated context is used as the lookup key; the selection module additionally conditions on the full current trajectory tau when ranking candidate guidelines.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: a query (context) is constructed at each timestep of the test trajectory (per-state retrieval), not once at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative: retrieval (context identification + dictionary lookup + top-k guideline selection) is performed at every timestep of the test episode (fixed per-step schedule).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered at each timestep. The only gating is whether the generated current context matches an existing context key in the dictionary (if no match, an empty guideline set is returned and the agent proceeds without guidelines); there is no uncertainty/confidence/learned-router trigger.
reranking: Yes (LLM-based selection acts as a reranker): when more than k guidelines exist under the matched context, the LLM guideline-selection module M_select is prompted to choose the top-k most relevant guidelines for the current trajectory. It is an LLM/instruction-based selector, not a cross-encoder.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank/select only: the LLM selection module filters the candidate guideline set down to top-k relevant ones conditioned on the context and current trajectory. No decomposition, compression, or reason-in-documents distillation at test time (the distillation into concise guidelines happens earlier, during offline induction).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill descriptions are indexed; retrieved units are distilled guidelines, not tool docs).
index_content_separation: Partial: the dictionary uses a lightweight generated 'context' key to index into heavier guideline content, so context matching acts as a coarse index before the LLM selects the actual guideline text. Not a formal progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content design.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no live tool index or integration protocol; static frozen guideline store).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the matched context and the selected top-k context-aware guidelines are inserted into the LLM agent's action-generation prompt so the agent conditions its next action on the retrieved guidance. No training-signal use, no skill execution, no latent-token injection.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-act within the interactive rollout: at each timestep the agent identifies the current context, retrieves/selects relevant guidelines, and then generates an action conditioned on them (built on a ReAct/SoM base agent). Not inside MCTS/tree search; not one-shot plan-time exemplars.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-action within a rollout (each environment step): retrieval and guideline injection occur once per agent action step (each ReAct think-act decision).
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL reuse of the retrieved guideline (injected as-is into the prompt); no per-case revision at test time. Exception: in the out-of-domain transfer experiment (WebShop->WebArena-Shopping) an additional GPT-4-Turbo grounding module re-aligns the WebShop guidelines to the new domain's observations (LLM-prompted adaptation).
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy-as-guideline: concise free-text conditional natural-language rules (a context description plus an actionable guideline), injected as text into the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: State-aware guideline/rule: a distilled, context-conditional natural-language rule (higher abstraction than a raw trajectory or single demonstration), describing the state/context in which a recommended action applies.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Context-conditioned selection as the primary robustness mechanism: by retrieving only guidelines whose generated context matches the current state and then LLM-selecting top-k relevant ones, AutoGuide avoids flooding the agent with irrelevant guidelines (the failure mode of ExpeL's all-guidelines prompting). The top-k cap also limits distractor overload (ablation shows k too large causes 'overthinking'). No dedicated retriever-aware training or self-reflection relevance evaluator.
memory_type: workflow/procedural-style guideline library (a context-keyed dictionary of distilled natural-language guidelines). Not episodic raw-trajectory memory, skill-library of executable programs, graph, or latent memory.
write_back: False at deployment. The guideline dictionary is written once during the offline induction phase and is frozen at test time; the system does not store new experiences/guidelines online during evaluation.
online_growth: No: the retrievable guideline store does not grow during test-time deployment; it is fixed after offline induction (test tasks are non-overlapping with the offline/training tasks).
write_back_trigger: Offline induction only (effectively 'never' during deployment): guidelines are written during the offline phase from contrastive success/failure trajectory pairs; no per-step, on-success, reflective, or human-validated write-back occurs at test time. (Reflexion, when combined, adds intra-task feedback to the prompt but is not written into the guideline store.)
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure contrastive: guidelines are extracted by contrasting a higher-return (success) trajectory tau+ against a lower-return (failure) trajectory tau- for the same task, identifying the deviation timestep and generating a guideline that captures the desirable vs undesirable action in that context. Failures are used contrastively (not stored as standalone corrective rules and not success-only).
memory_evolution_update: Dedup-merge during construction: an LLM context-matching step merges contexts describing the same situation expressed differently (reuse existing key) before appending the new guideline; otherwise append-only. No delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forgetting/pruning after writing.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval/guideline selection is prompted LLM-based context-keyed lookup plus LLM top-k selection, not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private store. The guideline dictionary is built and used by one agent pipeline. (It generalizes/transfers across domains in the out-of-domain experiment, but there is no multi-agent or cross-framework shared-memory mechanism.)
benchmarks: ALFWorld; WebShop; WebArena (focused on the Reddit domain for main experiments; WebArena-Shopping for out-of-domain transfer); real-world multi-modal websites: GitHub, Google Flights, Coursera.
benchmark_family: embodied (ALFWorld); web (WebShop, WebArena / WebArena-Reddit / WebArena-Shopping, and real-world multi-modal websites GitHub/Google Flights/Coursera).
baselines: ReAct; ExpeL (non-contextual all-guidelines prompting; guidelines-only variant); Reflexion (and ReAct+Reflexion, ExpeL+Reflexion, AutoGuide+Reflexion combinations); ReAct with varying numbers of in-context examples (1/2/4/6-shot); Set-of-Marks (SoM) GPT-4V agent for the multi-modal real-world web tasks.
key_metrics: Task success rate (SR, %) and, for WebShop, average reward; multi-modal real-world web results reported as success counts (e.g., x/30).
headline_result: On WebArena-Reddit (GPT-4-turbo base), AutoGuide reaches 47.1% success rate vs ExpeL 21.8% and ReAct 8.0%. Also: ALFWorld SR 79.1% (vs ExpeL 59.0%, ReAct 54.5%) and 88.1% with Reflexion; WebShop reward 73.4 / SR 46% (vs ReAct 66.4/30%, ExpeL 60.9/35%).
ablations: (1) Component ablation on WebShop: ReAct 30% -> ReAct+CI (context identification only) 36% -> ReAct+GES (guideline extraction+selection without contexts) 37% -> full AutoGuide (CI+GES) 46%, showing both context summaries and contextual guideline selection are needed. (2) Top-k ablation on WebShop: k=0 (ReAct) 30%, k=1 42%, k=2 46%, k=3 47% (best), k=5 43% (degrades from overthinking). (3) ReAct in-context-example count on WebShop (1/2/4/6-shot: 30%/35%/37%/38%; AutoGuide 46% beats all and avoids token-limit blowup). (4) Out-of-domain transfer: guidelines from WebShop applied to WebArena-Shopping raise SR from 10.2% (ReAct) to 20.4% (AutoGuide, with a GPT-4-Turbo grounding module). (5) AutoGuide+Reflexion complementarity (inter-task vs intra-task knowledge).
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task metrics (success rate / reward) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, context-match accuracy, or guideline-completeness) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final task SR / reward). Process is examined only qualitatively via trajectory case studies (Figure 4 comparing ReAct/ExpeL/AutoGuide action selection) rather than quantitative step-wise retrieval/planning accuracy.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively rather than via formal cost metrics: AutoGuide's concise guidelines compress offline data and stay within GPT context limits where many-shot ReAct (>6-shot) exceeds the GPT-3.5-turbo token limit; selecting only top-k context-relevant guidelines reduces prompt burden vs ExpeL's all-guidelines prompting. Per-step retrieval adds extra LLM calls (context identification + selection) each timestep, but no latency/API-cost/token-count numbers are reported. [uncertain]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: top-k guideline selection with k=2 in the main ALFWorld and WebShop experiments (Tables 7-8); WebShop ablation sweeps k in {0,1,2,3,5} with k=3 best. Budget is implicitly capped by selecting a small k and by injecting only the matched context's guidelines rather than the whole store.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a benchmark contribution; evaluation sizes noted: ALFWorld extracted from first 100 training tasks; WebShop induced from 50 sampled training tasks and evaluated on 100 test tasks (max 15 actions, top-3 search results); WebArena-Reddit and WebArena-Shopping (98 shopping tasks with a product in the intent template); real-world web: GitHub 30 tasks, Google Flights 20, Coursera 20.
builds_on: ReAct (reasoning+acting base agent); ExpeL (offline natural-language guideline extraction from experiences); Reflexion (test-time self-feedback, used complementarily); Set-of-Marks (SoM) prompting for multi-modal GPT-4V agents.
contrasts_with: ExpeL (explicitly positioned against: ExpeL provides ALL guidelines non-contextually whereas AutoGuide retrieves only state/context-relevant guidelines; AutoGuide reports substantial improvements over ExpeL's non-contextual all-guidelines prompting); demonstration-based in-context learning / many-shot ReAct (raw-trajectory exemplars hit context limits and plateau); plain ReAct (no offline knowledge); Reflexion (intra-task self-feedback vs AutoGuide's inter-task guideline knowledge, shown complementary).
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience-distillation planning). Sits in the lineage of experience/guideline-distillation methods for LLM agents (ExpeL -> AutoGuide), advancing from non-contextual all-guidelines prompting to state-conditional retrieval of distilled guidelines; complementary to self-reflection lines (Reflexion) and ReAct-style interactive agents.
